items.title: Nearby Iranian positions (implied operational area), Iran: Iranian strategist Mehdi Kharratiyan called for Iran to abandon its religious prohibition on nuclear weapons and prepare to become a nuclear power, while expanding bilateral and trilateral relations with Russia and China.
items.description: Iranian strategist Mehdi Kharratiyan called for Iran to abandon its religious prohibition on nuclear weapons and prepare to become a nuclear power, while expanding bilateral and trilateral relations with Russia and China.
items.rawSummary: Nuclear negotiations between Iran and the United States are stalemated as a senior Iranian strategist publicly called for Tehran to pursue nuclear weapons capability, while the fragile ceasefire persists amid intermittent US strikes and internal Iranian rifts.
items.analysis: Secretary of State Rubio described the Iran deal as a work in progress and stressed President Trump will not accept a bad agreement, even as US military strikes persist—including new strikes on a site threatening forces and traffic in the Strait of Hormuz—and oil markets whipsawed, with WTI crude initially falling 4% to $92 before rising toward $95 per barrel on strike-driven uncertainty. The Wall Street Journal reported that the UAE secretly carried out dozens of airstrikes against Iran during the war, coordinating with the US and Israel, targeting military and energy sites and continuing until after the ceasefire was announced, intensifying tensions between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh over the regional response. Vice President JD Vance said Iran wants a deal and to reopen the Strait, acknowledged that ceasefires can have messy flare-ups from lower-level communication but maintained the ceasefire is broadly holding, even as CNN reported that Iran used bulldozers to reopen at least 50 tunnel entrances across 18 underground missile sites, restoring access to missiles sealed by earlier US-Israeli strikes. Iranian and US accounts of the nuclear negotiations have diverged sharply; Iranian officials indicated they will not accept President Trump’s most recent demands, and accounts subsequently suggested Iran is becoming increasingly stubborn and offering few nuclear concessions, dampening earlier expectations that a deal was near. In a further hardening of Iran's stated position, an Iranian strategist called for Tehran to abandon its religious prohibition on nuclear weapons and to prepare to become a nuclear power while deepening ties with Russia and China. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent offered a stark characterization of the leadership landscape, stating the US did not pursue regime change but had decapitated the first and second levels of Iran's leadership, leaving third-level officials in charge. Meanwhile, a public rift emerged between President Pezeshkian and the IRGC over internet controls, and internet access gradually returned after an 88-day nationwide blackout. Separately, NBC News reported that the US F-15 shot down over Iran earlier in the conflict, which triggered a massive evacuation operation, was struck by a Chinese-made MANPADS likely donated to Iran at the start of the war.

items.title: United States (Diplomatic focus on Iran), United States: The New York Times reported Trump has repeatedly needled Vance over his Iran stance, a mission to Pakistan, vacations, and personal moments including a fumbled trophy.
items.description: The New York Times reported Trump has repeatedly needled Vance over his Iran stance, a mission to Pakistan, vacations, and personal moments including a fumbled trophy.
items.rawSummary: President Trump has hardened U.S. demands in nuclear talks with Iran, insisting on a ban on both developing and purchasing a nuclear weapon and demanding free passage through the Strait of Hormuz, while economic pressures mount at home.
items.analysis: Diplomatic efforts with Iran entered a more hardline phase after President Trump reviewed a draft deal and requested amendments that impose stricter conditions for handling Iran's enriched uranium, clearer language on freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, and an explicit prohibition on developing or purchasing a nuclear weapon. Axios reported that U.S. officials expect an Iranian response within days. Trump has simultaneously described the U.S. as being 'close to a very good deal' and declared he is 'in no hurry,' repeating that if demands are not met the situation will be ended 'in a different way,' a stance that has intensified since the conflict began over three months ago. Domestically, economic pressures are mounting: real disposable income fell 1.1 percent year-over-year in April and the personal savings rate dropped to 2.6 percent, while inflation continues to erode purchasing power. Internal administration tensions have also surfaced, with the New York Times reporting Trump's private criticisms of Vice President Vance’s political future and habits, even as Trump publicly praised Vance for uncovering fraud and suggested a balanced budget could be near.

items.title: Islamabad, Pakistan, Pakistan: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said a 'true friendship' is developing between the U.S. and Pakistan.
items.description: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said a 'true friendship' is developing between the U.S. and Pakistan.
items.rawSummary: With a U.S.-Iran agreement still stalled over disputed provisions and a signing venue unconfirmed, U.S. Defense Secretary Hegseth emphasized a growing friendship with Pakistan even as an Iranian lawmaker cautioned Islamabad against trusting Washington.
items.analysis: The draft 'Islamabad agreement' mediated by Pakistan remained stalled over two key provisions, with Iran's Tasnim news agency warning the deal could collapse if Washington did not end what Tehran calls obstruction. Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reiterated that nothing is final, Tehran continues to deeply distrust the United States, and any implementation depends on verification, while leaked terms outlined eased U.S. shipping restrictions, restoration of Iranian commercial shipping in the Gulf within a month, and potential UN Security Council backing but left the Strait of Hormuz under Iranian and Omani control and a U.S. military pullback undefined. In a separate domestic statement, Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif explicitly rejected joining the Abraham Accords, citing fundamental ideological clashes and deep distrust of Israel. President Trump later revealed that he agreed to the talks at the request of Pakistan's Field Marshal Asim Munir, whom he described as 'somebody we greatly respect,' and unconfirmed Pakistani sources claimed Islamabad has been chosen as the signing venue for a memorandum, though neither Washington nor Tehran has confirmed. Amid the deadlock, Iranian MP Mottaki warned Pakistan to be careful about U.S. intentions, while U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said a 'true friendship' is developing between Washington and Islamabad, underscoring the clashing narratives around the mediation.

items.title: Japan, Japan: Defense Minister Shinjirō Koizumi rejected the 'new militarism' label and expressed serious concern over China's expanding military capabilities and insufficient transparency, while emphasizing Japan's door is open for candid dialogue.
items.description: Defense Minister Shinjirō Koizumi rejected the 'new militarism' label and expressed serious concern over China's expanding military capabilities and insufficient transparency, while emphasizing Japan's door is open for candid dialogue.
items.rawSummary: Japan is navigating an oil import shock from the Strait of Hormuz closure, a deepening demographic crisis with a record population decline, surging gold exports linked to smuggled bullion, its first contribution to a NATO fund, and defense statements addressing China’s military transparency.
items.analysis: Japan’s crude oil imports collapsed 59% month-on-month in April after the Iran war severed over 90% of Middle Eastern supply, prompting two emergency reserve releases that lowered stockpiles to 202 days of coverage; imports are expected to rebound sharply in May from alternative sourcing, underscoring the acute vulnerability of importers reliant on the Strait of Hormuz. The 2025 census recorded a population decline of 3.1 million—the largest five-year drop since records began—with births at a record low of 705,000 and nearly 30% of the population aged 65 or older, while the child population had already fallen for the 45th consecutive year and government debt reached 204% of GDP. Gold exports surged 35.6% year-on-year in fiscal 2025 to a record $25.5 billion, which the Finance Ministry attributes to an outflow of gold previously smuggled to avoid the 10% consumption tax. In a separate development, Japan contributed approximately $14.7 million to NATO’s Ukraine procurement fund for non-lethal equipment, its first such contribution. Meanwhile, Defense Minister Shinjirō Koizumi rejected the ‘new militarism’ label, noting Japan lacks nuclear weapons and strategic bombers, while expressing serious concern over China’s expanding military capabilities and lack of transparency, and calling for candid dialogue.

items.title: Southwestern Iran, Iran: NBC, citing three people with knowledge, reported the downed F-15E was likely struck by a Chinese-made shoulder-launched missile, possibly an FN-6; the incident triggered a rescue mission in which several other aircraft were damaged or destroyed.
items.description: NBC, citing three people with knowledge, reported the downed F-15E was likely struck by a Chinese-made shoulder-launched missile, possibly an FN-6; the incident triggered a rescue mission in which several other aircraft were damaged or destroyed.
items.rawSummary: A US F-15E shot down over southwestern Iran last month was likely hit by a Chinese-made shoulder-launched missile, possibly an FN-6, triggering a dangerous rescue mission that damaged or destroyed other aircraft; China may also have supplied Iran with a YLC-8B early-warning radar.
items.analysis: NBC reported that the US F-15E Strike Eagle downed over southwestern Iran last month was probably struck by a Chinese-made shoulder-launched surface-to-air missile, possibly an FN-6, according to three people with knowledge of the matter. The shootdown prompted a risky rescue operation in which several additional aircraft were damaged or destroyed. The report further indicated that China may have provided Iran with a YLC-8B long-range early-warning radar, which could enhance Tehran's ability to detect stealth aircraft. If confirmed, the combined missile and radar transfers would mark a notable broadening of Chinese military support to Iran amid its ongoing hostilities with the United States.

items.title: New Delhi, India: India finalizes a $629 million deal to sell BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles to Vietnam and is close to signing a similar agreement with Indonesia.
items.description: India finalizes a $629 million deal to sell BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles to Vietnam and is close to signing a similar agreement with Indonesia.
items.rawSummary: India faces a depreciating rupee and energy price pressures as it finalizes a $39 billion Rafale fighter jet deal with France and a $629 million BrahMos missile export to Vietnam, while President Trump offers '100%' support and Prime Minister Netanyahu highlights India's strong backing for Israel.
items.analysis: India confronts a depreciating rupee, elevated energy costs from the Iran conflict, and a Moody's growth forecast cut to 6%, while The Telegraph reported that the Trump administration's simultaneous outreach to China and Pakistan adds diplomatic pressure. During his May 23–26 visit, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Prime Minister Modi, and President Trump later said India could rely on the US '100%'; Rubio dismissed a reporter's question about a 'hellhole' post as anonymous trolling, and the visit concluded with the Quad Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi. In separate defense developments, India finalized a $39 billion request for 114 Rafale fighter jets from France and a $629 million deal to sell BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles to Vietnam, and is nearing a similar agreement with Indonesia, reinforcing its defense diversification and export ambitions. Separately, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu noted India's strong public support for Israel, contrasting it with delegitimization elsewhere.

items.title: Beijing, China: China's crude oil imports fell to multi-year lows, with May volumes tracking at the weakest since 2016 and annual projections averaging 10.9 million barrels per day for 2026, reversing the stockpiling trend that previously absorbed surplus oil and now capping global price upside.
items.description: China's crude oil imports fell to multi-year lows, with May volumes tracking at the weakest since 2016 and annual projections averaging 10.9 million barrels per day for 2026, reversing the stockpiling trend that previously absorbed surplus oil and now capping global price upside.
items.rawSummary: Beijing is recalibrating defense diplomacy, expanding nuclear capabilities, and making rare gestures toward Taiwan, while its sharply declining oil demand is capping global crude prices.
items.analysis: China's defense minister will skip a high-level security forum for the second consecutive year, reflecting Beijing's cautious approach to military-to-military contacts with the United States amid internal purges and despite a recent Trump-Xi summit. In parallel, China has rapidly expanded its nuclear arsenal and is moving toward a counterforce posture out of concern that U.S. first-strike capabilities could undermine its deterrent. A notable diplomatic exception saw China permit a Taiwanese minister-level official to attend an APEC event on its soil, deviating from its usual obstruction of Taiwanese international participation. Separately, China's crude oil imports have plunged to historic lows, with May volumes tracking at about 6.6 million barrels per day—the weakest since 2016—reversing years of aggressive stockpiling that once absorbed global surplus and supported prices; this retrenchment is now limiting upward pressure on crude markets even amid supply shortages elsewhere. The broader economic and energy realignment adds a new layer to China's strategic posture, while regional assessments also note that a potential U.S. suspension of arms sales to Taiwan could shake confidence and that Tomahawk missile delivery delays to Japan might hamper Tokyo's deterrence planning.

items.title: Strait of Hormuz area (Bandar Abbas vicinity), Iran: The Institute for the Study of War assessed that hardline IRGC officials remain unwilling to make meaningful concessions in negotiations, and Western media reported that Iran may have used a Chinese-made man-portable air defense system against U.S. aircraft during the war, citing three individuals familiar with the matter.
items.description: The Institute for the Study of War assessed that hardline IRGC officials remain unwilling to make meaningful concessions in negotiations, and Western media reported that Iran may have used a Chinese-made man-portable air defense system against U.S. aircraft during the war, citing three individuals familiar with the matter.
items.rawSummary: While negotiations remain stalled despite an unofficial draft that would give Iran greater transit authority in exchange for $12 billion in frozen assets, Iran sought to present the Revolutionary Guards' strait management as a new status quo, and Western media cited reports that Chinese-made MANPADS were potentially used against U.S. aircraft during the war.
items.analysis: President Trump’s declaration that the naval blockade was lifted was immediately contradicted by both Iranian state media and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who confirmed the blockade remains and that the United States controls the strait. The U.S. tightened economic pressure through Treasury sanctions on front companies while U.S. Central Command prepared to clear Iranian mines north of the Musandam Peninsula, and the Wall Street Journal detailed extensive UAE airstrikes on Iranian infrastructure that Saudi Arabia feared could trigger wider attacks on energy sites. Iranian state media reported a still-unofficial draft understanding that would grant Iran authority to classify, inspect, and potentially restrict vessels transiting the strait in return for a U.S. commitment to release $12 billion in frozen assets, but the text is not final and negotiations are deadlocked, with the Institute for the Study of War assessing that IRGC hardliners are unwilling to make meaningful concessions. Iran also sought to frame the IRGC’s direct management of strait transit as the new status quo, while Western media reported it may have used a Chinese-made man-portable air defense system against U.S. aircraft during the war. Oman’s Ministry of Defense alerted mariners to a suspected Iranian Maham-3 mine in its territorial waters, underscoring the persistent threat to navigation.

items.rawSummary: Hard-line Iranian officials continue to reject diplomatic overtures, with a senior parliamentarian stating talks will fail and that the nuclear issue was never on the table, as the IRGC displays new naval assets and the country's tourism sector collapses.
items.analysis: Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf hardened the official stance by demanding concrete results and asserting confidence in victory, a posture echoed by IRGC Brigadier General Yadollah Javani who declared that Trump faces only 'bad' or 'worse' options. Now, National Security Committee member Esmail Khosari has publicly stated that talks with Washington will not produce a deal, called the U.S. president a liar, and claimed the nuclear issue 'was never on the table,' with current negotiations focused on ending the war, compensation, U.S. withdrawal, and lifting the naval blockade. Tehran has already rejected Washington's core demand to transfer enriched uranium stocks, and the IRGC showcased its asymmetric naval capabilities with a military parade and the unveiling of a new fast-attack boat. Meanwhile, a special command center has been formed to plan Supreme Leader Khamenei's funeral, and a small but influential hard-line faction inside parliament and the Supreme National Security Council actively works to derail diplomacy. The head of Iran's Travel Agencies Association reported that tourism has fallen 'below zero,' underscoring the severe economic toll of ongoing tensions.
